interface.title: Bacterial Growth Analyzer
interface.stage_of_work: Data processing and analysis of plate-reader growth curves
interface.what_it_is_for: Load plate-reader OD-vs-time data into a well layout, subtract blank-well background, fit growth models (logistic, exponential, Baranyi, Gompertz, custom) over chosen time windows with confidence intervals, and detect growth phases automatically.

data.note: example_spreadsheet.xlsx loaded with the '24 well rows 4 column 6' layout. Rows A and B are empty (None). Wells C1, C6 and D1 stay flat and were used as blanks. C2–C5 show growth that peaks near t≈13 and drops sharply at t≈20.5.

tree.general: Turn raw optical-density time courses from a multi-well plate into corrected growth curves and fitted growth parameters
tree.specific: Upload a plate-reader OD spreadsheet, subtract blank wells, fit growth models and detect growth phases
declared_gaps: Fitting a user-defined ODE system to the corrected curve (define variables, ODE expressions and parameters for a time window, solve and fit with confidence intervals, then view a summary plot of all ODE fits). The tool and plan name this as a main goal, but the run stopped right after adding an empty ODE fit (screens/072.webp).
Combining replicate groups with arithmetic operations (Add/Subtract/Multiply/Divide) to make the operated data that later steps use (Advanced Mode, Operations tab). This was never opened.

Background subtraction for several groups at once, e.g. treatment and control groups each with their own blanks (Advanced Mode). This is a variant of the background phase, and only the single-group Basic Mode path was run.

features.name: Windowed curve fit with model choice, initial guesses/bounds, CI and parameter statistics
features.general: Fit a chosen model to part of a time series, setting starting values and limits, then inspect the fit, confidence band and parameter significance
features.specific: Manual Fit N: start/end time → model (Exponential, Logistic, Baranyi, Lag-Exponential-Saturation, Gompertz, Custom Function, Automatic Fit) → initial guesses and 'Use bounds for …?' → Fit Model → R², residual variance, fitted curve, 'Confidence Intervals with Standard Deviation' plot, and a parameter table (estimate, std. error, t, p, fit quality). The default initial guesses do not suit every model: for Baranyi, the default X0≈0 gave a degenerate fit.
steps: add a fit with start/end time
choose a model
adjust initial guesses (e.g. set Baranyi's X0 by hand) and turn on bounds for any parameter
press Fit Model
read R², the CI plot and the parameter table, and treat huge standard errors or exploding CI bands as a poorly identified fit
repeat for more windows or models, or delete a fit
serves_tasks: Fit a sigmoid model over a chosen time window and read parameters with uncertainty
Fit another model over a different window and check whether its parameters are identifiable

features.name: Automatic phase segmentation by slope/derivative
features.general: Split a time series into phases where its smoothed derivative or slope changes, and mark the change points on the plot
features.specific: Phase Detection: method Thresholded Derivative (Savitzky-Golay smoothing window, polynomial order, derivative threshold, min distance between breakpoints) or Slope-Based (slope window size, slope threshold) → Detect Phases → 'Detected N phase(s)' with shaded phases, change-point lines and a derivative trace. On noisy growth curves the defaults over-segment (20 phases for Thresholded Derivative, 50 for Slope-Based here).
steps: choose a detection method
set smoothing/window and threshold parameters; the defaults over-segment noisy data, so widen the window, raise the threshold or the minimum breakpoint distance
press Detect Phases
inspect the shaded phases and change points, and re-tune if the count is far above the expected few phases
serves_tasks: Detect phase boundaries automatically from changes in the smoothed curve's derivative or slope

screens_never_reached: Operations tab (Advanced Mode: combine groups with arithmetic operations): the sidebar button was visible (screens/062.webp), but I ran out of my ~100-action budget before opening it
ODE Analysis results: I added an ODE fit (Fit 1, t=0–27.83, screens/072.webp) and saw a 'Variables & ODEs' heading, but did not define equations, solve, or reach the summary plot
Custom Function and Automatic Fit model modes in Fitting: seen in the model dropdown (screens/045.webp) but not tried
'Custom' well format and the 'No Fitting (Use Average)' blank model: seen in their dropdowns but not tried
Multi-group background subtraction (Advanced Mode): Basic Mode only allows a single Group 1
not_done: Defining and solving a custom ODE system and comparing its fitted parameters with uncertainty: I stopped right after pressing 'Add ODE Fit' because the action budget was used up
Combining groups with arithmetic operations (Operations tab): not visited, also because of the action budget

Thresholded Derivative phase detection with the smoothing window dragged to 15 showed no result or message after two presses of Detect Phases (screens/064.webp, screens/065.webp). This is a dead end at window 15, not a failure of the method: the replay, using the default window 5 / threshold 0.005, got 'Detected 20 phase(s)' (check/screens/040.webp, check/screens/041.webp). Slope-Based with default settings reported 50 phases (screens/069.webp). Neither method was tuned toward clean lag/exponential/stationary phases.

The Baranyi fit over t=0–14 fitted poorly (R² 0.9488). Its confidence-interval plot blew up to about ±8000 OD (screens/060.webp), so the parameters are poorly identified. The replay showed that the default X0≈0 guess does not move at all (R² −0.69), and X0=0.003 converges (R² 0.9553) but still gives q0≈1.26e7 with a huge SE and a CI axis of ±100k (check/screens/034.webp, check/screens/036.webp). No converging second model (e.g. Gompertz) was fitted for comparison.
The 'Add New Fit' time fields reset when the start time changes. The first attempt made a 0–0 fit (Manual Fit 2), which I left in place. Fit panels collapse after each rerun.
Pressing 'Generate Background Configuration JSON' the first time ran the subtraction and drew the corrected plots instead of showing the JSON. The JSON editor only appeared after a second press.
